spins.publish_note: The Cheebacabra is the recording project of Seattle-based producer, photographer, and preschool teacher Paul Cheever (aka Cheeba). At 18 years old, Cheever was pulled into the inner circle of the legendary Dust Brothers production team who redefined the art of sampling with artists such as Beck and Beastie Boys. After three years with them, doing everything from cleaning bongs to editing tracks for the Fight Club score, Cheever began to focus on his own recordings. The first Cheebacabra album, Metamorphosis, was released in 2003. Drawing on influences such as Herbie Hancock, DJ Premier, and Weather Report, The Cheebacabra attempts to combine the organic and soulful instrumentation of ‘70s jazz-funk and fusion with the crisp drums and head-bobbing production of ‘90s hip-hop.

spins.publish_note: Soft Machine are an English rock band from Canterbury, Kent. The band were formed in 1966 by Mike Ratledge, Robert Wyatt, Kevin Ayers, Daevid Allen and Larry Nowlin. Soft Machine were central in the Canterbury scene; they became one of the first British psychedelic acts, and later helped pioneer progressive[1][2] and jazz rock. Soft Machine's lineup has undergone many changes, and has included Andy Summers, Hugh Hopper, Elton Dean,[3] John Marshall, Karl Jenkins, Roy Babbington and Allan Holdsworth. As of 2025, the current lineup consists of John Etheridge, Theo Travis, Fred Thelonious Baker and Asaf Sirkis. The band's name originates from William S. Burroughs's novel The Soft Machine.

spins.publish_note: Leftfield are a British electronic music group formed in London in 1989, a duo of Neil Barnes (born 6 August 1960[2]) and Paul Daley (the latter formerly of The Rivals and A Man Called Adam). The duo was influential in the evolution of electronic music in the 1990s, with Mixmag describing them as "the single most influential production team working in British dance music".[1] As with many of their contemporaries, such as The Chemical Brothers and Fatboy Slim, Leftfield are notable for their use of guest vocalists in their works. Among them are Toni Halliday on "Original", Johnny Rotten on "Open Up", Djum Djum on "Afro-Left", Earl 16 and Cheshire Cat on "Release the Pressure", and Grian Chatten of Fontaines D.C. on "Full Way Round". The term progressive house was coined to define their style, a fusion of house with dub and reggae.

spins.publish_note: Atmospheric ambient soundscapes meet strong post-rock build-ups Kairos is the sophomore album from Berlin trio AUSKLANG, following the monumental, critically-acclaimed Chronos (Past Inside the Present, 2020). Throughout its eight movements, Fabian Koppri, Benjamin Sohn, and Simon Ansing play with concepts of relative time and entropy through a masterful balance of melodic post-rock and layered ambient bliss, adorning an understated frame of guitar, bass, and drums with complex, ever-evolving arrangements, ranging from glitchy electronics to classically inspired orchestrations. Kairos is one of two words that the ancient Greeks had for 'time'; Chronos which refers to chronological or sequential time, and Kairos which signifies a good or proper time for action, which is qualitative.

spins.label: Bastard Jazz Recordings
spins.publish_note: Seattle's own Manatee Commune (aka Grant Eadie) makes his long-awaited return to Bastard Jazz with his fourth album, 'Simultaneity'. Lush and vibrant production is familiar to his previous works, though Eadie has significantly matured in the activation of space and character. A step away from standard songwriting, and a total disassociation from lyrics at all, has made this record closer to the ambient genre than anything Manatee Commune has released, all the while keeping one solid foot in the realm of dance music.

spins.publish_note: Originally founded in the spring of 1996. The name refers to the Dutch word "de ramp" which means "disaster" or "catastrophe". Between 1997 and 2003, ['ramp] released a string of albums and played a couple of concerts in the Netherlands, the UK, and Germany before Parsick went entirely solo in 2009. the album presented here was assembled from roughly two hours worth of music, recorded live in concert at dechenhöhle iserlohn, a grotto in the south-west of germany's industrial heartland, the ruhr district. markus reuter was invited to join ['ramp] for the concert that was to take place on 26th october 2002 but had to cancel his performance at the very last minute due to other commitments. Performed and recorded live in concert at Dechenhöhle Iserlohn on 26th October 2002. Mastered in December 2008 some of the music turned out to be oppressive to an extent that quite a few people decided to walk out of the cave after the first set, never to be seen again.
